_note: One row per shell. Wave 0 held only the hand-authored flag; wave 1A adds the kit fields. Kit fields (only when tier is not 'none'): tier (none|S|T|O|E), company (a kit file in this folder), ep (the string kit_ep holds, e.g. ca01), chainId (optional, names kit_<chainId>_out; defaults to ep), ambient (two person keys from the kit's staff), stub (the shared stub knot; defaults to ep), setPiece (name in the kit's setPieces, or null), attack (true for a full shell with an attack half: adds the kit_attack_done mapping), stepAway (the row is the one source: written to social.awarenessEpisode.stepAway), stepAwayBark (optional host line on the step-away mapping), keyMessage (optional: the id of the message in the shell's first triage set that the episode's key lesson rides on; the tool writes outcome.messageGlobals {<id>: kit_key_caught} on that set and declares the generic global kit_key_caught, the one name every episode's stubs and host ink read; the validator errors if the global clashes with the set's own result names), hostLine (optional, true when the shell has a host layer-2 line: declares kit_<ep>_host_said, the line's said-once flag; independent of keyMessage), override (optional: deep-merges into the kit before building, keyed sources by id and staff by person; a value of null deletes that key; used only to pin a test fixture to its frozen placeholder positions and timings). A row with handAuthored true is never written by a generator (it is touched only by apply_training_room.py). A row with fixture true is a test scenario, not a course shell. A row for a test scenario that is not a fixture (test_ca01_panel) is regenerated like a course shell: --kit rebuilds its kit content from the set piece and refuses to erase hand-written kit content.
